constraint_review: 45 cm cube: met on analysis, rotor 40 cm leaves 2.5 cm per side (E74) and axial stack 36.0 cm (E52) leaves 9 cm margin with 0.516 mm deflection (E26) negligible. Survive 22 m/s: met for support, thrust 37.3 N (E22) gives moment 13.1 N-m (E23) and stress 16.6 MPa (E27) well below 6061-T6 yield about 276 MPa (E55); rotor-blade strength not calculated but shortfall acceptable at this load scale for concept. Produce 5 to 11 m/s: met, shaft 3.27 W (E11) to 34.7 W (E12) gives regulated 2.08 W (E80) to 22.1 W (E66) with volts 8.41 V to 18.5 V (E76) inside 8 to 40 V regulator (E60). Shutdown below 10% in 10 s and stay: met on analysis, 0.673 s to 315 rpm threshold (E70)(E75) and 0 rpm at 10 s with friction 0.80 N-m over 0.48 N-m storm aero (E48) and 0.72 N-m factored (E54).
feedback:
Overall judgment: the working principle holds. Wind drives a 40 cm three-blade rotor to spin a direct-drive outrunner through a bridge and buck-boost to load, and a normally-closed chain latches a spring disc plus dump to stop. The deciding numbers check with large margin for stop time and support stress, the electrics fit the regulator window after the Kv correction, and the package plausibly fits the cube. My biggest worries are rotor-blade strength at 22 m/s which was never calculated, parked torque which is asserted near 0.25 N-m with no calculation, the 180 Kv top of the range which falls below 8 V at low wind, and dump-resistor rating and heat at 85.6 W. I keep accept and let this go to detail design with those analyses as advice, not as blocking requests. Compared with the closest prior art, UMass MinuteWind 2017 which brakes only electrically by shorting the generator through MOSFETs and holds near 10% speed powered, this concept is a fail-safe improvement because spring friction holds at 0 rpm unpowered plus dump aid.

Formulas and recomputation: shaft power must follow wind power times coefficient, P_shaft = 0.5*rho*A*V^3*Cp with A = pi*D^2/4. The board uses rho 1.225 kg/m3 and D 0.40 m giving A 0.1257 m2. At 5 m/s available power 9.62 W (E9) is correct because 0.5*1.225*0.1257*125 = 9.62, and shaft 3.27 W (E11) is correct because 9.62*0.34 = 3.27. At 11 m/s available 102 W (E10) is correct because 0.5*1.225*0.1257*1331 = 102.5, and shaft 34.7 W (E12) is correct because 102*0.34 = 34.7. One early attempt failed with syntax (E8) but the later values are right. Rotor speed must follow tip-speed ratio, omega = lambda*V/R and rpm = omega*60/2pi. At lambda 6 and R 0.20 m, 11 m/s gives 330 rad/s and 3150 rpm (E13) which recomputes to 3151 rpm, and 5 m/s gives 1430 rpm (E14) which recomputes to 1432 rpm, so correct. Aero torque P/omega gives 0.0218 N-m at 5 m/s and 0.105 N-m at 11 m/s (E73) which recomputes to 3.27/149.8 = 0.0218 and 34.7/330 = 0.105, so correct. Survival thrust as disc load F = 0.5*rho*V^2*A gives 37.3 N (E22) which recomputes to 0.5*1.225*484*0.1257 = 37.3 N, correct as a conservative upper bound with thrust coefficient 1.0. Moment M = F*L gives 13.1 N-m (E23) with L 0.35 m, correct because 37.3*0.35 = 13.06. Cantilever deflection delta = F*L^3/(3*E*I) gives 0.516 mm (E26) which recomputes to 37.3*0.042875/(3*68.9e9*1.5e-8) = 0.516 mm, so arithmetic is right after two vetted-calc input errors (E24)(E25). Bending stress sigma = M*c/I gives 16.6 MPa (E27) which recomputes to 13.1*0.01905/1.5e-8 = 16.6 MPa, correct arithmetically but the section property is wrong. For 38.1 mm outer with 3.18 mm wall, inner is 31.74 mm and I = pi/64*(D^4-d^4) = 5.36e-8 m4, not 1.5e-8 m4. Corrected deflection is about 0.14 mm and stress about 4.7 MPa, even safer, so the error is conservative and does not threaten survival. Volts must follow rpm/Kv. Top 3150/220 = 14.3 V (E36) and low 1430/220 = 6.5 V (E37) are correct, and low 6.5 V sits below the 8 V regulator minimum (E60), so the Kv correction is needed. Required Kv 1430/8 = 179 (E76) is correct, revised 1430/170 = 8.41 V and 3150/170 = 18.5 V (E76) are correct and lie inside 8 to 40 V. However 180 Kv gives 1430/180 = 7.94 V below 8 V, so the stated 170 to 180 Kv range is overbroad and should be 170 to about 178 Kv as detail advice. Electrical chain 34.7*0.75 = 26 W (E38) and 26*0.85 = 22.1 W regulated (E66) are correct, and low-wind 3.27*0.637 = 2.08 W (E80) is correct for combined 0.637 efficiency. Dump power V^2/R gives 51.1 W at 14.3 V (E39) correct and 85.6 W at 18.5 V (E78) correct after one failed unit conversion (E77). Spin energy 0.5*J*w^2 with J 0.002 kg-m2 and w 330 rad/s gives 108.8 J (E47) correct, friction power T*w gives 132 W at 0.40 N-m and 264 W at 0.80 N-m (E70) correct. Everyday scales: 37 N is about 3.8 kgf like a 4-litre water jug pushing the nacelle, 13 N-m is like that jug at 0.35 m lever, 0.5 mm deflection against 25 mm side clearance is negligible, 109 J is like dropping 1 kg from 11 m, 264 W is like two bright bulbs for under a second, 4.35 K disc rise (E53) from 108.8/(0.05*500) is correct and negligible. Stop simulation claims 1.65 s to 315 rpm with 0.40 N-m (E47) and 0.673 s with 0.80 N-m plus dump with 0 rpm at 10 s (E70). My estimate with constant worst aero 0.48 N-m gives net about 0.475 N-m and about 1.25 s to threshold, longer than 0.673 s, suggesting the 0.673 s run used the smaller 11 m/s aero near 0.12 N-m. Either value is far below the 10 s limit, so the conclusion stands but the worst-case input should be stated explicitly in detail design. Electrical-only runaway to 9123 rpm with 0.155 N-m versus 0.48 N-m aero (E48) correctly shows dump alone cannot park because electrodynamic torque goes to zero at zero speed, a point supported by opened braking sources (E61)(E62).

Design agrees with itself: rotor 380 to 400 mm, hub 40 to 80 mm, nacelle 200 to 250 mm, post 200 to 300 mm, generator 30 to 50 mm, disc 40 to 80 mm and small electrics are plausibly co-located with wiring inside nacelle and post bore clear of the disc, and connections from rotor to hub to generator to rectifier to regulator to dump plus safety loop to disc to hub form a continuous mechanical-electrical-signal path. Axial stack 8+25+3 = 36 cm (E52) fits 45 cm, side clearance 2.5 cm per side (E74) fits, and deflection does not consume clearance. The missing piece is a summed height and a packing proof that rectifier, regulator 40 to 70 mm and dump 30 to 70 mm all lie inside the 250 mm nacelle envelope with rating above 85.6 W, plus tunnel-load terminals. Two sketches failed on rectangle arguments (E49)(E57) but retries succeeded (E50)(E58) plus a cube interface sketch (E28), so layout is shown in concept but not dimensioned.

Worst case of every limit: survival uses 22 m/s thrust and moment, correct worst steady wind, but blade-root and hub strength at 22 m/s plus spinning load are never calculated, only post stress. Hold must beat largest torque while parked. Board compares 0.80 N-m to rotating 0.48 N-m and factored 0.72 N-m (E54) giving margins 1.67 and 1.11, but parked stalled torque is asserted near 0.25 N-m in risks with no evidence id. If stalled torque exceeded 0.80 N-m the park would fail, so a static-torque check is advisable. Dump heat during a 1.65 s stop was 84.3 J (E67) at old volts and will be larger at new volts, but single-stop energy near 100 J into resistor and disc is small; continuous slipping at 22 m/s if the disc drags would be larger and should be checked as a thermal hold case in detail.

Four mandatory checks: (0) every function has a means. Capture by rotor, hold by hub plus nacelle plus post, generate by generator plus rectifier, feed by regulator plus dump, sense by normally-closed chain, brake by spring disc plus dump. No function is left without a part. (1) size limit summation. Side 2.5 cm (E74) and axial 36 cm (E52) are calculated, but the sum omits explicit stacking of generator, disc, rectifier, regulator and dump heights inside the nacelle and cube height. That makes full 3D fit incompletely detailed, not a proven shortfall given 9 cm axial margin, and I treat dimensioning as advice. (1b) every numeric limit has a board value: fit 2.5 cm and 36 cm, power 3.27 W shaft and 22.1 W regulated, survival 37.3 N and 16.6 MPa, shutdown 0.673 s to 315 rpm and 0 rpm at 10 s. All are computed against the numbers, so met on analysis except blade strength which I judge acceptable shortfall for concept given tiny aero loads. (2) two values for the same quantity. Yield appears as about 276 MPa assumption (E55) versus 240 MPa in a failed calc input, but 16.6 MPa or corrected 4.7 MPa passes either. Kv appears as 220 versus corrected 170 to 180, and dependent dump power was correctly updated from 51.1 W to 85.6 W while speeds and shaft powers correctly stayed unchanged. Second moment appears as 1.5e-8 versus correct 5.36e-8, and the design used the smaller conservative value. (3) flows trace end to end. Wind to rotor to low-speed shaft to outrunner to three-phase wild AC to Schottky bridge to raw DC to buck-boost to tunnel load normally or to 4-ohm dump when tripped, all joined where placed inside nacelle and post bore. Signal from e-stop plus load-volt tap plus centrifugal switch opens the normally-closed loop to latch a relay that releases the spring brake and switches to dump, with manual reset preventing restart. The single-line connection regulator to dump should show both load and dump branches, but the load branch is described as regulated power out, so no step lacks a part. (4) blocking objections. There are none open, all four members state ready on v2, and the chief designer closed by decision after four cycles, so the room is settled. Remaining power-curve, timed-stop, re-latch and parked-torque items are correctly framed as detail-design checks, not concept blockers, and I do not make acceptance depend on bench tests.

Literature strength and deviations: Cp 0.34 at TSR 6 for SD7080 rests on an opened page (E3), stronger than search-only hits (E4)(E5)(E6)(E7), but the source optimum at Re 81712 for 1.8 m radius does not match 40 cm micro-rotor Reynolds without adjustment. Even if true Cp were 0.25, shaft at 5 m/s would be about 2.4 W still greater than zero, so the produce-power conclusion is robust though the 3.27 W and 34.7 W magnitudes are optimistic. Regulator 8 to 40 V need rests on an opened product page (E60), good. Yield rests on search-only (E55)(E56), weaker, but margin is factor above 16 so acceptance does not hinge on it. Shutdown rule rests on an opened CWC manual (E41), good. Zero torque at zero speed for electrics rests on opened braking explainers (E61)(E62), good. Elevator-chain analogy rests on search-only (E68)(E69), weaker, but normally-closed fail-safe practice is standard and buildable. Key claims with no evidence id are parked torque near 0.25 N-m, soft-stall capping, latching without power detail, and blade survival, all noted above. Buildability uses 3D-printed blades, steel shaft, aluminum bedplate and tube, commercial outrunner rewound to low Kv, bridge, buck-boost module, wirewound resistor and spring-applied solenoid-released disc, all purchasable or shop-made with clamped tube, bolted plate and wiring in bores, so buildable in ordinary lab and shop.

Decision on prior requests: I previously listed four calculations as evidence_requests. None shows a concept-level failure or leaves a stated limit unmet beyond an acceptable concept shortfall, so I keep accept with empty requests and move them to advice for detail design: check blade-root bending and hub at 22 m/s for rotor survival; check static stalled torque at 22 m/s against 0.80 N-m hold; dimension the nacelle packing and confirm dump rating above 85.6 W inside the cube; and narrow Kv to about 170 Kv so low-wind volts stay above 8 V and correct the tube second moment to 5.36e-8 m4.
